Short title extent and commencement

THE PROTECTIVE DUTIES ACT, 1950
THE PROTECTIVE DUTIES ACT, 1950
ACT No: LXI of 1950
[23rd October, 1950]
An Act to enable the immediate imposition of protective duties of
customs on imported goods
WHEREAS it is expedient to enable
the Central Government to impose with immediate effect ‑protective duties
of customs on goods produced or manufactured‑outside Pakistan and
imported into Pakistan where such imposition is urgently necessary in the
interest of industries established in Pakistan;
It is hereby enacted as follows :‑
1.Short title extent and commencement.‑(1) This Act may be
called the Protective Duties Act, 1950.
(Subs. ibid., for the original sub‑section
(2) (with effect from the 14th October, 1955).) [(2) It extends to the whole of Pakistan.]
(3) It shall come into force at
once.

Power of Central Government to impose of duties of Custom

ACT No: LXI of 1950

imported into Pakistan where such imposition is urgently necessary in the
interest of industries established in Pakistan;
It is hereby enacted as follows :‑
2. Power of Central Government to impose of duties of Custom. (Subs. by the Protective Duties (Amdt.) Act, 1951 (34 of
1951), s. 2, for the original sub‑section (1).) [(1) If the Central Government is of the opinion that it is
urgently necessary to provide for the protection of the in terests of any
industry established in (Subs. by the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960
(21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch., for "the Provinces or the Capital of the
Federa tion" (with effect from the 14th October, 1955).) [Pakistan]. the Central Government
may, by notification(For such notification, see Gaz. of P., Ext., 1952, p 103; and
ibid 1955, pp 461‑462 and 1478, 1573 and 1979; and ibid., 1956, pp. 1369‑1745
and Gaz. of P. 1959, Ext. p. 1593.)
in the official Gazette‑
(a) impose on any goods produced
or manufactured in any country outside Pakistan and imported into (Subs. by the
Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch.,
for "the Provinces or the Capital of the Federa tion" (with effect from
the 14th October, 1955).)
[Pakistan] a duty of customs of such amount (Ins. by the Finance Ordinance, 1960 (25 of
1960), s. 4 (with effect from the 1st July, 1960).) [and for such period] as it thinks fit; or
(b) change the nature of a duty
of customs, imposed on any goods produced or manufactured in any country
outside Pakistan and imported into (Subs. by the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960
(21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch., for "the Provinces or the Capital of the
Federa tion" (with effect from the 14th October, 1955).) [Pakistan], into protective:
Provided that no notification
shall be made under this sub‑section unless the Central Government is
first satisfied, upon a report submitted to it in this behalf by the Tariff Com mission
set up by the Central Government, that the industry in respect of which the
report is submitted should be protected.]
(2) Every duty imposed under
sub-section (1) shall be deemed to be a duty leviable under the Tariff Act,
1934, and shall be in addition to any duties imposed under that Act or any
other law for the time being in force (Certain original words omitted ibid. (with effect from the
1st July, 1960).)* * * XXXII
of 1934.

Power to alter rates of protective duty and to extend the duration of the protection and the continuance of certain protective duties

THE PROTECTIVE DUTIES ACT, 1950
THE PROTECTIVE DUTIES ACT, 1950
ACT No: LXI of 1950
[23rd October, 1950]
An Act to enable the immediate imposition of protective duties of
customs on imported goods
WHEREAS it is expedient to enable
the Central Government to impose with immediate effect ‑protective duties
of customs on goods produced or manufactured‑outside Pakistan and
imported into Pakistan where such imposition is urgently necessary in the
interest of industries established in Pakistan;
It is hereby enacted as follows :‑
3. Power to alter rates of protective duty and to extend the duration
of the protection and the continuance of certain protective duties. (Subs. ibid., for the original section 3 (with effect from the
1st July, 1960).) [(1) If,
after such enquiry as it thinks necessary the Central Government is satisfied
that the duty imposed on any goods under sub‑section (1) of section 2
(altered, where necessary, in the manner hereinafter provided) has become
unnecessary or excessive or that it is too low to provide adequate protection
to the industry concerned in Pakistan, it may, by notification in the official
Gazette, reduce or raise the duty to such extent and for such period (which may
be extended from time to time but by not more than three years at any one time)
as it thinks fit.
(2) On the expiration of the
period specified in any noti fication issued under sub‑section (1) of
section 2 or sub‑section (1) of this section, whichever is the later,
there shall be levied and collected on the goods referred to therein customs duty
at the rates for the time in force under the Tariff Act, 1934, and the
provisions of the said Act and any other law for the time being in force
relating to the levy and collection of the duty of customs shall apply
accordingly XXXII of 1934.
(3) All duties described as
`protective' in the third column of the First Schedule to the Tariff Act, 1934,
as in force on the thirtieth day of June, 1960, shall continue to be levied and
col lected on and from the first day of July, 1960 as if the said duties had been
imposed under this Act. XXXII of 1634]

Powers to make rules

THE PROTECTIVE DUTIES ACT, 1950
THE PROTECTIVE DUTIES ACT, 1950
ACT No: LXI of 1950
[23rd October, 1950]
An Act to enable the immediate imposition of protective duties of
customs on imported goods
WHEREAS it is expedient to enable
the Central Government to impose with immediate effect ‑protective duties
of customs on goods produced or manufactured‑outside Pakistan and
imported into Pakistan where such imposition is urgently necessary in the
interest of industries established in Pakistan;
It is hereby enacted as follows :‑
4. Powers to make rules.‑(1) The Central Government may, by
notification in the official Gazette, make rules for the purpose of carrying
into effect the provisions of this Act.
(2) In particular and without
prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power such rules may prescribe the
conditions subject to which any goods shall be deemed to be produced or
manufactured in a particular country for the purposes of this Act.

3A. Powers of the Tariff Commission. (New
section 3A ins. by the Protective Duties (Amdt.) Ordinance, 1962 (30 of 1962),
s. 2.)[The Tariff Commission
shall have all the powers of a civil court while trying a suit under the Code
of Civil Proce dure, 1908, in respect of the following matters, namely Act V of
1908:‑
(a) summoning and enforcing the
attendance of any person and examining him on oath;
(b) requiring the supply of any
information and production of any document which may be useful for the conduct
of its enquiry.]
